claim: For an irreducible unitary carrier and an invariant positive self-adjoint operator on End(H) with kernel span{I}, every complex matrix A of rank at most d-k obeys the finite Green/cutoff lower bound [d B(k)/k^2+1/lambda_1]^-1, with projector overlap ||Pi_j P||_HS^2<=k^2 b_j/d for any rank-k projection into the right kernel. The high-frequency mass can be sharpened from k to k-k^2/d.
supplied_inputs: Carrier representation, invariant spectrum and multiplicities, and integer 1<=k<d.
proof: Right-kernel trace identity, complex weighted Cauchy-Schwarz on the traceless subspace, Schur partial trace, and a Schmidt-rank projector mass bound. No positivity assumption on A.
evidence: Independent derivation in green_lower.txt; finite checks also appear in the integrated near_full.py diagnostic. The proof is analytic; finite checks are not proof.
falsifier: A valid rank-k P and invariant spectral projector violating the k^2 b/d overlap, or a complex A violating the Green/Cauchy-Schwarz converse under the stated hypotheses.

Explicit radial resistance tapers and occupation caps attain the stated orders. For m=2, Lambda(d_N-k)~1/log(d_N/k) whenever k=o(d_N).
supplied_inputs: N, fixed m, integer branch/rank budget Q, and the specified generator normalization.
costs: Mathematical rank-energy bounds only. No circuit runtime, synthesis, precision, physical preparation, or external operational equivalence is audited here.

evidence: Independent notes in green_lower.txt, radial_upper.txt, su2_log_profile.txt, and regime_overlap.txt. `python3 outputs/research/sol_semiclassical_memory/verify_near_full.py` reports 64 arbitrary-kernel projection fixtures and 81 radial/cap comparator checks. All finite checks are diagnostic only.
